Q4: Thermal Energy Storage for Process Heat Applications The National Solar Thermal Test Facility welcomed Scott Hume of the Electric Power Research Institute and Luke McLaughlin of Sandia National Laboratories during Sandia’s Concentrating Solar Power Seminar Series on Tuesday, Aug. 26, 2025. Thermal energy storage is a historic yet emerging technology that holds great promise to lower costs and boost the reliability of industrial process heat, particularly when paired with variable energy sources. TES technologies come in a variety of configurations, store heat in diverse ways and can be utilized for many different heating applications. Scott Hume and Luke McLaughlin facilitated an engaging session. Link: https://digitalops.sandia.gov/Mediasite/Play/b4acc93547d24b88b08dd6835863178f1d 12 3. SITE UTILIZATION SUMMARY & CUSTOMER PROFILE 3.1. Site Utilization During the Fiscal Year 2025 the NSTTF completed upgrades to its heliostat field communications hardware and completed a significant portion of the construction of G3P3. A breakdown at our solar furnace resulted in a reduction of our average site utilization during the year, yet we continued to serve a wide range of customers and support funded projects awarded to NSTTF researchers. Site utilization percentage is defined relative to the number of “good weather” days within a test period. While average site utilization for the NSTTF was down and 2025 brought a heavy monsoon season, usage at the NSTTF solar tower increased by 23% compared to Fiscal Year 2024 and is expected to increase further in Fiscal Year 26 with 2 new customers beginning test campaigns on the solar tower. Despite increased solar tower testing and weather slowing the pace of G3P3 construction throughout the year, testing of our gen 3 tower will begin in 2026. Additionally, operations at the furnace will start in Q2 2026. With all these activities, we are expecting 2026 to be a high usage year for the NSTTF. Our optics lab was our most utilized facility and achieved a utilization of 92% in Q4, further progressing our goal of delivering excellent optical metrology to support the concentrating solar industry, research, and education worldwide. Our solar simulator usage increased to 20% utilization while our heat transfer test stand usage went unchanged but is expected to increase with the expected arrival and installation of a molten salt test loop in 2026. 3.2.
